# Keyboard accessibility fixes for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers the code remediation for the keyboard-accessibility defects
found by the audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. The audit
report enumerates the exact defects per flow — focus is lost in modals, several
controls are unreachable with keyboard alone, and focus indicators are
inconsistent. After this epic, each of the four flows is fully operable by
keyboard with consistent, visible focus indication.

## Scope

- Remediate every keyboard-accessibility defect the audit enumerated across the
  four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission):
  - Eliminate focus traps and restore correct focus behavior when modals and
    dialogs open and close (focus moves into the modal on open and returns to
    the invoking control on close).
  - Make every control in the audited flows reachable and operable via
    keyboard alone, in a logical tab order.
- Make visible focus indicators consistent across the audited flows by aligning
  modal/dialog focus management and focus-indicator styling on shared
  patterns, so all controls in these flows render a uniform, visible focus
  indicator.
- Track each audit defect to resolution or explicit disposition.

Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given keyboard-only interaction (no mouse), when a user completes each of
  the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission), then the flow can be completed end-to-end with all
  controls reachable and operable — measured by a keyboard-only walkthrough of
  each flow against the audit defect list, with zero unresolved defects.
- Given a modal or dialog in any audited flow, when it opens and closes, then
  focus moves into it on open and returns to the invoking control on close,
  with no focus loss or focus traps — measured by the same walkthrough.
- Given any interactive control in the audited flows, when it receives
  keyboard focus, then a visible focus indicator is displayed consistently with
  the other controls across all four flows — measured by inspection of focus
  indicator rendering across the audited flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is resolved,
  or explicitly dispositioned with a documented rationale.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the keyboard
  operability and modal focus remediation in this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the focus-indicator consistency work in this epic.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed state of the four audited core Dashboard flows: the
conformance statement (VPAT) and the product documentation accessibility
statement. Two public-sector customers require an updated, published conformance
statement before renewal, so the published documentation — not just the code
fixes — is a deliverable of this strategy.

This epic starts only after the Dashboard keyboard accessibility fixes for the
four audited flows are complete, because the conformance claims must describe
the implemented, fixed state and be technically reviewed against it.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT so its conformance claims reflect the implemented keyboard
  operability and focus-indicator state of the four audited flows (project
  creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to match the same
  fixed state.
- Republish both documents through the Red Hat docs content process so the
  updated conformance statement is available to customers.

Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard
fixes require, and flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the completed keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited flows,
  when the VPAT is updated, then every conformance claim matches the
  implemented behavior of those flows — measured by technical review against
  the implementation, with the review sign-off recorded before republication.
- Given the updated VPAT, when it is republished, then the published
  conformance statement reflects the fixed state and is accessible to
  customers.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated and republished
  to reflect the same fixed state.
- The technical review of the conformance documentation against the
  implementation is complete and recorded prior to republication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review — this epic is the sole owner of that
  requirement.
